admission.justification: Signing every token was a real alternative with a real cost, and the rejection rests on a property of the selector rather than on convenience.

alternatives.option: Carry the walk's binding in the token without a signature, and refuse a token that names what a fresh request could not read
alternatives.reason: A token that can only re-select what the caller was already allowed to select gives a signature nothing to protect.

alternatives.option: Sign the token so a caller cannot alter it
alternatives.reason: A signature would protect integrity of a document whose only power is a re-selection the caller could make anyway.
alternatives.reconsider_when: a token could name a record or a tree the caller could not have selected in a fresh request, or a caller is shown to gain access by editing one.

consequences: Tokens stay short and readable; the selector refuses a seed the tree no longer holds (`selector_absent`) instead of trusting the token's contents.
context: A continuation token carries what a walk is bound to. A caller could edit it, so the packet had to decide whether the token needs a signature or only needs to name nothing a fresh request could not have selected.
decider: the developer, under D47, as MIK-R73@v1 rule 9 (inventory entry 151) states it
